# CloudThinker

> CloudThinker builds Frontier Investigation Agents. They find the root cause. You approve the fix. Products: Resolve (incidents), Review (code changes), Cyber (application security), Optimize (cloud cost), Customize (your rules, runbooks and tools) and Automation (scheduled and event-driven runs).

## Get started / Start here

- [CloudThinker Docs](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/index.md): Learn what CloudThinker's Frontier Investigation Agents do, get your first answer in about 10 minutes, and pick a product.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/quickstart.md): Connect one system read-only and have CloudThinker investigate an issue happening now, or an incident from last week, in about 10 minutes.
- [How CloudThinker Works](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/concepts.md): Learn the concepts behind every CloudThinker product, from organizations and connections to agents, skills, approvals, and memory.
- [Tutorial: Your First Investigation](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/tutorial/agenticops.md): Trace a restarting Kubernetes service through cloud metrics and recent code changes to one root cause, then review the fix CloudThinker proposes.

## Get started / Learn the basics

- [Agents](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/overview.md): Learn who answers your requests: the built-in CloudThinker assistant, the subagents it spawns, and the custom agents your team builds.
- [Home and Activity](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/activity.md): Clear what's waiting on you from Home, find any past agent report in Activity, and check today's automation runs.
- [Commands and Prompt Syntax](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/commands.md): Write requests CloudThinker understands, then save the ones you repeat as slash commands your whole workspace can run.
- [Glossary](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/glossary.md): Look up a plain definition of every CloudThinker term you meet in the app and these docs, with a link to the page that covers it

## Get started / Help

- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/troubleshooting.md): Find the fix for the most common CloudThinker problems, from sign-in and connections to approvals, products, Workers and the CLI.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/faq.md): Get quick answers on what CloudThinker does, what access it needs, how agent changes are approved, pricing, and where to get help.

## Get started / Work where you are

- [Slack Integration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/slack-integration.md): Connect Slack so your team can ask CloudThinker questions in channels and receive alerts and review summaries where they already work.
- [Microsoft Teams Integration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/teams-integration.md): Connect Microsoft Teams so your team can ask CloudThinker questions in team channels and receive alerts and review summaries as cards.
- [Google Chat Integration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/google-chat-integration.md): Install CloudThinker in Google Chat, map each space to a workspace, and ask questions, approve actions, and get alerts in chat.
- [CLI](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/overview.md): Install the CloudThinker CLI, log in, and run CloudThinker from your terminal, shell scripts, and CI pipelines.
- [CLI Authentication](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/authentication.md): Log in to the CloudThinker CLI from a laptop or over SSH, switch between workspaces, and give scripts and CI jobs a credential.
- [Agent CLI](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/agent.md): Run CloudThinker Agent in your repository to edit code locally and reach your cloud through workspace connections with approval.
- [Headless Chat](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/headless-chat.md): Send a prompt to CloudThinker from a script or CI job, pipe the answer, and collect long runs later by run ID.
- [CLI Reference](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/reference.md): Look up every cloudthinker command, flag, environment variable, exit code, and file path in one place.

## Products / Resolve / Get started

- [Resolve](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/overview.md): See how Resolve turns raw alerts into investigated incidents, approved fixes, and lessons, and find the page for each job.
- [Resolve Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/quickstart.md): Send a test alert to Resolve, watch Pulse group it into a cluster, and open the incident and its root-cause analysis.

## Products / Resolve / Set up

- [Resolve Integrations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/integrations.md): Connect the platforms Resolve listens to, reads from, and acts through, then check each one is ready before your next incident.
- [Connect Pulse Sources](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/setup.md): Connect a webhook, an AWS polling source, or a chat channel so your alerts reach Pulse, then confirm the first signal arrives.
- [Webhook Signals](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/webhook-integrations/overview.md): Send alerts from a monitoring tool into Resolve with a webhook, map their fields, and choose when CloudThinker investigates on its own.
- [Connect CloudWatch Alarms](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/webhook-integrations/cloudwatch.md): Route CloudWatch alarm state changes to Resolve through EventBridge, then confirm each alarm arrives in Pulse as a signal.
- [Add a Custom Signal Source](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/webhook-integrations/custom-source.md): Connect any system that can POST JSON to Resolve, capture one real event, and map its fields by clicking them.
- [Resolve Settings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/settings.md): Decide whether CloudThinker investigates incidents on its own, pause it during maintenance, and choose where its progress updates appear.

## Products / Resolve / Work incidents

- [Pulse Overview](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/overview.md): Learn how Pulse drops alert noise, groups related events into clusters, and hands only actionable problems to incident triage.
- [Signal Clusters](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/clusters.md): Triage Pulse clusters: understand their lifecycle and suppression, then acknowledge, assign, escalate, attach, snooze or resolve them.
- [Investigation and RCA](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/root-cause-analysis.md): Start a root-cause investigation on an incident, read the verdict and its evidence, and decide what to do next.
- [On-call and the Incident Room](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/oncall.md): Choose who Resolve brings into an urgent incident, open the Incident Room and Slack war room, and work the incident with CloudThinker.
- [Runbooks](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/runbooks.md): Give Resolve your team's fix procedures from Confluence, GitHub, GitLab, or Markdown uploads, and review every runbook action it takes.
- [Log an Incident Manually](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/manual-logging.md): Log an incident from a customer report or your own observation, attach evidence, and get a root-cause investigation started right away.

## Products / Resolve / Learn and improve

- [Resolve Insights](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/insights.md): Check how fast Resolve handles incidents, how often its diagnoses are right, and where Pulse and runbooks leave gaps.
- [Pulse Analytics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/analytics.md): Measure how well Pulse turns raw alerts into actionable clusters, and find the noisy sources worth fixing first.
- [Incident Memory](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/incident-memory.md): Learn what CloudThinker records from each investigation, how it reuses those notes on repeat failures, and how to confirm a fix held.

## Products / Resolve / Help

- [Resolve Troubleshooting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/troubleshooting.md): Find and fix the stage where Resolve stopped: alerts not arriving, clusters not forming, investigations stuck, or runbooks not running.

## Products / Resolve / Coming soon

- [Detectors](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/detectors.md): Preview Detectors, an upcoming Resolve feature that writes and tests checks for the incidents your alert rules miss.

## Products / Review / Get started

- [Review](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/overview.md): Get an AI review on every pull or merge request, with findings posted as comments in GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps or CodeCommit.
- [Review Setup](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/setup.md): Connect your Git provider, choose repositories and get your first AI review on a pull or merge request in about ten minutes.

## Products / Review / Set up

- [Provider Authentication](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/provider-auth.md): Authenticate GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps or AWS CodeCommit for Review, with the exact token scopes and webhooks each one needs.
- [Review Workspace](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/review-workspace.md): Triage reviewed changes, settle findings, apply fixes, and merge from the Reviews page without opening your Git provider.
- [Learnings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/convention-rules.md): Teach Review your team's standards from resolved findings and from the convention files already in your repository.
- [Review Extensions](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/extensions.md): Connect Jira, Confluence, Linear, Backlog or your Git provider's issues so Review checks each change against the ticket it implements.

## Products / Review / Use Review

- [Mention Commands](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/mention-commands.md): Re-run reviews, fix findings, and ask questions by mentioning @cloudthinker-ai in a merge request or pull request comment.
- [Auto-Resolve Conflicts](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/conflict-resolution.md): Detect merge conflicts on open MR/PRs and let CloudThinker resolve them in a follow-up MR/PR that you review and merge.
- [Pipelines](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/pipelines.md): Turn on pipeline analysis so every failed CI run gets a root-cause explanation and a suggested fix, without reading raw job logs.
- [Releases](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/releases.md): Analyze a release before you ship it, read its risks and next steps, and record an Approve or Hold decision your whole team can see.

## Products / Review / Insights and help

- [Review Insights](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/analytics.md): Track review quality, contribution and recurring finding domains across your team, and find what to coach next, from Review Insights.
- [Review Troubleshooting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/troubleshooting.md): Fix the common Review problems: no review on a PR, skipped reviews, Git provider auth errors, re-reviews and mention commands that get no reply.

## Products / Cyber / Get started

- [Cyber](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/cyber-overview.md): Learn how Cyber attacks your web apps and APIs, proves each finding with evidence, and helps you fix and retest it.
- [Cyber Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/cyber-quickstart.md): Register a staging app, verify its domain, add a test user, scope your first pentest to a few paths, run it at Safe intensity, then read the findings it proves.

## Products / Cyber / Run tests

- [Run a Pentest](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/pentest.md): Set up a pentest target, verify its domain, add test users and scope, then run it now or on a schedule and track the results.
- [Deep Dive Pentest](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/pentest-deep-dive.md): Run Cyber's most thorough pentest mode to find role, tenant, and multi-step flaws, with an optional credit limit for the run.
- [Handle CAPTCHA Logins](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/captcha.md): Configure CAPTCHA options so a Pentest password login can sign in, then confirm the run really tested behind the login.

## Products / Cyber / Results

- [Triage Security Findings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/cyber-findings.md): Read the proof behind each pentest finding, move it through your fix workflow, dismiss false positives, and start a fix with an agent.
- [Create Cyber Reports](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/cyber-reports.md): Export selected pentest findings as a PDF, write a custom report in your own format, and download or revise a run's full report.

## Products / Cyber / Help

- [Cyber Troubleshooting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/cyber-troubleshooting.md): Fix common Cyber problems: domain proof, test logins and CAPTCHA, blocked or failed runs, findings that won't move, and reports.

## Products / Optimize / Get started

- [Optimize](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/overview.md): Find savings in your AWS, GCP, or Azure bill, see what drives spend, and catch unusual cost changes for each cloud account.
- [Optimize Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/quickstart.md): Connect a cloud account read-only, run the first Optimize scan, read Cost Health and your first findings, and share a cost report.

## Products / Optimize / Explore spend

- [Cost Explorer](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/analytics.md): Compare completed monthly spend by service, region, or account, ask CloudThinker why a cost changed, and export the breakdown as CSV.
- [Cost Anomalies](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/anomalies.md): Review daily cost spikes for a cloud account, record what each one meant, and ask CloudThinker to find the cause

## Products / Optimize / Act on savings

- [Optimize Findings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/recommendations.md): Prioritize savings findings by evidence, move them through the workflow board, and record why a finding needs no action
- [Savings Estimates](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/savings.md): Read the Potential monthly savings total in Optimize, see which findings it counts, and keep the estimate accurate as your team works.
- [Optimize Reports](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/reports.md): Generate a cost report from saved Optimize data in one click, or schedule it to run daily, weekly, or monthly

## Products / Optimize / Help

- [Optimize Troubleshooting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/troubleshooting.md): Find and fix Optimize problems: billing access, scans with no data, findings you can't change, Implement on a read-only connection, anomalies, Cost Explorer, and reports.

## Products / Automation / Automation

- [Automation Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/automation/quickstart.md): Build a daily cost anomaly check that alerts a Slack channel, test it with Run now, and keep any write behind approvals.
- [Automations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/automation/automations.md): Run agent instructions on a schedule, a webhook call, a repository event, or a probe, and review every run and approval.
- [Autonomous Operations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/automation/autonomous-agents.md): Set the limits for agent work that runs with no one at the keyboard, and get told when it fails, waits, or changes itself.

## Platform / Connections

- [Connections](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/overview.md): Connect your cloud, data, and tooling so agents can investigate them, and keep that access scoped, verified, and rotated.
- [Amazon Web Services](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/aws.md): Connect an AWS account with a read-only IAM role so agents can investigate compute, storage, identity, cost, and monitoring.
- [Google Cloud Platform](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/gcp.md): Connect a Google Cloud project with a read-only service account so agents can investigate compute, GKE, BigQuery, identity, and cost.
- [Microsoft Azure](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/azure.md): Connect Microsoft Azure with a service principal so CloudThinker can read resources, audit access, and report spend in Optimize.
- [Firebase](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/firebase.md): Connect Firebase with a service-account key so CloudThinker can inventory apps, audit security rules, and check deploy state.
- [Cloudflare](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/cloudflare.md): Connect Cloudflare with an API token so CloudThinker can review zones, traffic analytics, firewall events, and Workers.
- [Vercel](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/vercel.md): Connect Vercel so CloudThinker can triage failed deployments, read runtime logs, and audit domains and aliases
- [Netlify](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/netlify.md): Connect Netlify so CloudThinker can check deploy health, audit forms, and inventory projects, with every change going through your Approvals
- [Heroku](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/heroku.md): Connect Heroku so CloudThinker can review apps, dynos, logs, add-ons, and pipelines through a read-only connection
- [Render](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/render.md): Connect Render so agents can review services, deploys, logs, metrics, and datastores, with every deploy or change going through your Approvals.
- [DigitalOcean](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/digitalocean.md): Connect DigitalOcean so agents can inventory Droplets, apps, databases, and Kubernetes, review network exposure, and read billing.
- [Fly.io](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/flyio.md): Connect a Fly.io organization so agents can list apps, check machine state and placement, and audit volumes with a read-only token.
- [GreenNode](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/greennode.md): Connect GreenNode so agents can read vServer, VKS, vLB, vDB, and storage resources and run changes through the GreenNode CLI under your Approvals
- [FPT Cloud](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/fptcloud.md): Connect FPT Cloud with a personal access token so agents can inspect VMs, disks, networks, tags, and activity and run approved VM changes
- [OpenStack](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/openstack.md): Connect an OpenStack project so agents can inventory servers, volumes, networks, and quotas, flag waste and drift, and run approved changes
- [VMware vCenter](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/vmware.md): Connect vCenter so agents can inventory VMs, hosts, and datastores, audit snapshots and capacity, and run VM changes through approvals
- [Kubernetes](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/kubernetes.md): Connect a Kubernetes cluster with a read-only kubeconfig so agents can triage failing pods, check node pressure, and review RBAC
- [Rancher](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rancher.md): Connect Rancher with an API key so agents can list managed clusters, projects, and nodes, check health, and review who has access
- [Pulumi](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/pulumi.md): Connect Pulumi Cloud over OAuth so CloudThinker can inventory stacks, search managed resources, and review policy violations
- [HCP Terraform](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/terraform.md): Connect an HCP Terraform organization to review workspaces and recent run statuses, with workspace changes through your Approvals
- [SSH](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/ssh.md): Connect your servers over SSH so CloudThinker can check disk, memory, processes, services, and logs with key-based login
- [HashiCorp Vault](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/vault.md): Connect HashiCorp Vault so agents can check health, list secret keys, audit policies, and issue dynamic credentials through your Approvals
- [Keycloak](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/keycloak.md): Connect a Keycloak realm so agents can audit users, clients, roles, groups, and auth flows, and make identity changes through your Approvals
- [Backstage](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/backstage.md): Connect Backstage so agents can read your Software Catalog for ownership, dependencies, and metadata gaps, and manage locations after approval
- [Okta](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/okta.md): Connect Okta so agents can review user access, investigate sign-ins, and manage CloudThinker-owned groups through your Approvals
- [PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/postgresql.md): Connect a PostgreSQL database so agents can find slow queries, suggest indexes, and check vacuum, locks, and replication health
- [CockroachDB](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/cockroachdb.md): Connect CockroachDB so agents can read schemas, run bounded queries and plans, and change rows through your approvals
- [MySQL](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mysql.md): Connect a MySQL database so agents can inspect schemas, indexes, table health, and slow queries with a read-only user
- [MongoDB](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mongodb.md): Connect MongoDB or Atlas so agents can inspect databases, collections, indexes, and query plans in read-only mode
- [Redis](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/redis.md): Connect Redis so agents can inspect memory, key sizes, expiration, clients, and command latency with a read-only ACL user
- [ClickHouse](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/clickhouse.md): Connect ClickHouse so CloudThinker can explore schemas, check table health, and rank slow queries with analytical SQL
- [Apache Cassandra](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/cassandra.md): Connect Apache Cassandra so CloudThinker can audit keyspaces, check ring health, read rows, and make approved single-row changes
- [Snowflake](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/snowflake.md): Connect Snowflake so CloudThinker can break down warehouse credits, rank slow and failing queries, and review storage overhead
- [Databricks](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/databricks.md): Connect Databricks so CloudThinker can explain failed job runs, spot idle clusters, and explore notebooks and Unity Catalog
- [Neon](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/neon.md): Connect Neon with OAuth so CloudThinker can map projects and branches, inspect schemas, and audit slow queries
- [Supabase](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/supabase.md): Connect Supabase with OAuth so CloudThinker can review projects, schemas, migrations, and logs, and run changes through approvals
- [Elasticsearch](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/elasticsearch.md): Connect Elasticsearch so agents can search logs, read mappings, run ES|QL, and check shard and cluster health with read-only access
- [OpenSearch](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/opensearch.md): Connect OpenSearch so agents can check cluster health, inspect indices and shards, search documents, and explain relevance, read-only
- [InfluxDB](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/influxdb.md): Connect InfluxDB 2 or 3 so agents can list buckets or databases, flag infinite retention, and run bounded Flux or SQL reads
- [Microsoft SQL Server](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mssql.md): Connect SQL Server or Azure SQL so agents can map your tables, read and aggregate rows, and change single rows through your Approvals
- [Pinecone](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/pinecone.md): Connect a Pinecone project so agents can inspect indexes and namespaces, search records, and upsert through your Approvals
- [Apache Kafka](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/kafka.md): Connect Confluent Cloud or self-hosted Kafka so agents can inspect topics, read messages, check throughput, and debug Flink SQL
- [RabbitMQ](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rabbitmq.md): Connect RabbitMQ through its Management HTTP API so agents can check queue depth, consumer lag, dead letters, and node alarms
- [Flespi](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/flespi.md): Connect Flespi with an API token so agents can look up telematics devices, channels, messages, and streams through Flespi's MCP server
- [Grafana](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/grafana.md): Connect Grafana with a Viewer service account so agents can search dashboards, query metrics and logs, and check alert rules
- [Prometheus](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/prometheus.md): Connect a Prometheus-compatible endpoint so agents can run PromQL, find down scrape targets, and read firing alerts
- [Datadog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/datadog.md): Connect Datadog with an API key and a scoped application key so agents can search logs, metrics, monitors, traces, and incidents
- [New Relic](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/newrelic.md): Connect New Relic with a User API key so agents can run NRQL, check service health, and triage open issues and alerts
- [Dynatrace](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/dynatrace.md): Connect a Dynatrace environment so agents can run DQL, investigate open problems, review vulnerabilities, and find affected entities
- [AppDynamics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/appdynamics.md): Connect an AppDynamics Controller so agents can find slow business transactions, triage health-rule violations, and trace bottlenecks
- [Coralogix](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/coralogix.md): Connect Coralogix so agents can triage incidents, search logs and traces, query metrics, and find broken parsing rules
- [SigNoz](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/signoz.md): Connect SigNoz so agents can find slow operations, search logs and traces, and audit alert rules with a Service Account API key
- [Honeycomb](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/honeycomb.md): Connect Honeycomb with OAuth so agents can rank failing endpoints, run BubbleUp, and follow a trace to the span that failed
- [Splunk Observability](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/splunkobservability.md): Connect Splunk Observability Cloud so agents can read APM service health, exemplar traces, metrics, and SignalFlow results
- [Sumo Logic](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/sumologic.md): Connect Sumo Logic so agents can search logs, check monitors and collectors, and triage Cloud SIEM insights with a read-only Access Key
- [Graylog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/graylog.md): Connect Graylog so agents can check cluster health, list streams and index sets, search messages, and count them by field
- [Zabbix](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/zabbix.md): Connect Zabbix so agents can triage active problems, read host metrics and logs, and schedule maintenance through your Approvals
- [Better Stack](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/betterstack.md): Connect Better Stack with OAuth so agents can check monitors, open incidents, on-call coverage, and per-source logs
- [Rollbar](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rollbar.md): Connect Rollbar projects with access tokens so agents can rank top errors, tie them to deploys, and update an item
- [Sentry](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/sentry.md): Connect Sentry with OAuth so agents can search issues, read events and traces, and tie new errors to a release
- [Langfuse](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/langfuse.md): Connect a Langfuse project so CloudThinker can investigate LLM traces, costs, evaluation scores, and prompt versions
- [PostHog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/posthog.md): Connect PostHog so CloudThinker can triage tracked errors, read flags and insights, and answer usage questions with HogQL
- [Splunk Platform](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/splunkplatform.md): Connect Splunk Cloud Platform or Splunk Enterprise so CloudThinker can run read-only SPL searches and review indexes and saved searches
- [Braintrust](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/braintrust.md): Connect Braintrust so CloudThinker can compare experiment scores, read monitor views, and check project settings with one API key.
- [LangSmith](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/langsmith.md): Connect LangSmith so CloudThinker can find failed or costly LLM runs, inspect traces, and review dataset and experiment results.
- [UptimeRobot](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/uptimerobot.md): Connect UptimeRobot with its Read-only API key so CloudThinker can report down monitors, uptime history, and recent incidents.
- [Microsoft Clarity](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/clarity.md): Connect Microsoft Clarity so agents can answer traffic and engagement questions and pull matching session recordings
- [GitHub](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/github.md): Install the CloudThinker GitHub App so agents can read repositories, pull requests, and Actions runs, and Review can comment
- [GitLab](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/gitlab.md): Connect GitLab.com or self-managed GitLab so agents can read projects, merge requests, and pipelines, and Review can comment
- [Bitbucket](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/bitbucket.md): Connect Bitbucket Cloud so agents can read repositories, pull requests, and pipelines, and Review can comment on pull requests
- [Azure DevOps](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/azure-devops.md): Connect an Azure DevOps project so agents can read repos, pull requests, and builds, and Review can comment on pull requests
- [Jenkins](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/jenkins.md): Connect your Jenkins server so agents can read jobs, builds, logs, and test results, and trigger builds through your Approvals
- [CircleCI](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/circleci.md): Connect CircleCI so agents can triage failed pipelines, find flaky tests, validate config, and rerun workflows with approval
- [Buildkite](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/buildkite.md): Connect Buildkite so agents can track pipeline health, triage failed builds from logs, and retry or unblock jobs with approval
- [Docker Hub](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/dockerhub.md): Connect Docker Hub so agents can inventory repositories, compare pulls and push age, inspect tags, and update descriptions
- [ArgoCD](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/argocd.md): Connect Argo CD so agents can find out-of-sync and degraded apps, read events and logs, and sync an app after approval
- [AWX](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/awx.md): Connect Ansible AWX so agents can find failed jobs, inspect inventories and projects, and launch job templates after approval
- [SonarQube](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/sonarqube.md): Connect SonarQube so agents can explain failed quality gates, triage issues and security hotspots, and find untested code
- [GitGuardian](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/gitguardian.md): Connect GitGuardian so agents can triage secret incidents, trace exposed credentials to their sources, and check honeytokens
- [Harness](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/harness.md): Connect Harness so agents can check delivery health, diagnose failed executions, review cloud cost data, and edit resources through your Approvals
- [AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/aws-codecommit.md): Connect AWS CodeCommit so agents can read repositories and pull requests, and so Review can comment on your pull requests
- [Semgrep](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/semgrep.md): Connect Semgrep so agents can scan files for security issues, write and test custom rules, and read your AppSec Platform findings
- [PagerDuty](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/pagerduty.md): Send PagerDuty incident events to Resolve with a signed webhook, so CloudThinker can open an incident and start a root cause analysis
- [Rootly](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rootly.md): Connect Rootly so agents can triage open incidents, review alerts, and file the follow-up action items an incident leaves behind
- [ServiceNow](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/servicenow.md): Connect a ServiceNow instance so agents can review incidents, changes, problems, and CMDB items, and file updates through approvals
- [Atlassian](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/atlassian.md): Connect Jira and Confluence so agents can search issues and pages, pull ticket context into work, and file approved updates
- [Jira Service Management](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/jsm.md): Connect Jira Service Management Operations so agents can triage alerts, check on-call coverage, and work the alert lifecycle
- [Backlog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/backlog.md): Connect Backlog by Nulab so agents can read issues, milestones, wikis, and pull requests, and update tickets with your approval
- [monday.com](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/monday.md): Connect monday.com so agents can review boards, find stalled items, read updates, and change items through your Approvals
- [Linear](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/linear.md): Connect Linear so agents can search issues, projects, and cycles, flag blocked work, and update issues through your Approvals
- [Notion](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/notion.md): Connect Notion so agents can search your pages and databases, answer from your docs, and keep runbooks and postmortems current
- [ClickUp](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/clickup.md): Connect ClickUp with OAuth so agents can triage lists, review workload and status age, and change tasks after approval
- [Asana](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/asana.md): Connect Asana with your own OAuth app so agents can review project health and workload, and change tasks after approval
- [HubSpot](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/hubspot.md): Connect HubSpot with OAuth so agents can search contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, and summarize your sales pipeline
- [FireHydrant](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/firehydrant.md): Connect FireHydrant so agents can review open incidents, Signals alerts, severity, and which team owns each service
- [FortiGate](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/fortigate.md): Connect a FortiGate firewall so agents can check device health, licenses, and interface traffic, and change configuration with approval
- [Prowler](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/prowler.md): Connect Prowler so agents can review failed security findings, exposed resources, and compliance status across your cloud accounts
- [Wazuh](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/wazuh.md): Connect Wazuh so agents can investigate alerts and agents, test log lines, and change rules, decoders, and agents through your Approvals
- [Drata](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/drata.md): Connect Drata so agents can review failing tests, control readiness, and personnel gaps, and make changes after approval
- [MCP](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mcp.md): Connect your own MCP server so CloudThinker agents can call its tools next to the built-in connections.

## Platform / Customize

- [Customize](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/customize.md): Shape how CloudThinker works in your workspace with custom agents, skills, knowledge, credentials, notifications, and approvals.
- [Custom Agent Quickstart](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/quickstart.md): Build a custom agent in about 10 minutes once AWS is connected: add a runbook skill, create the agent, connect it, set approvals, test it.
- [Skills](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/overview.md): Turn your team's procedures and rules into skills agents apply on their own in Chat, Review, Incident, and Assessment.
- [Custom Skills](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/custom-skills.md): Create a workspace skill, choose where agents can use it, and confirm it changes their output in Chat, Review, Incident, or Assessment.
- [Skill Format](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/skill-format.md): Write a SKILL.md file that uploads cleanly and that agents follow: frontmatter fields, zip layout, limits, and a complete example.
- [Knowledge Base](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/knowledge.md): Upload runbooks, policies, and web pages into a knowledge base so CloudThinker answers from your own documents.

## Platform / Approvals

- [Approvals](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/approvals/overview.md): Decide which agent writes run on their own, which wait for a person, and which never run, and answer approval requests.
- [Approval Rules](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/approvals/rules.md): Find, review, accept, and edit the Rules that let an agent write run on its own, wait for a person, or never run
- [Approval Mode](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/approvals/approval-mode.md): Choose Manual or Auto for the workspace, each run type, one Automation, or one chat, and see what each choice does
- [Approvers and Activity](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/approvals/approvers.md): Choose who answers each approval card, require a second person, allow break-glass, and audit what each Rule decided

## Platform / Workspace settings

- [Workspace Settings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspace-settings.md): Find every workspace setting in one place: what each tab controls, who can change it, and where to learn more.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspaces.md): Create, switch, configure, and delete workspaces so each team or environment keeps its own connections, agents, and history.
- [Workspace Members](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspace-users.md): Add teammates to a workspace, set their workspace role, and control what each person can view, run, and change.
- [Workspace Branding](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspace-branding.md): Put your logo and company name on PDF exports and shared links, and your chart colors on PDFs and in-app artifacts, for one workspace.
- [Credentials](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/credentials.md): Store API keys and tokens once so agents can use them in commands, without anyone pasting a secret into chat.
- [Notifications](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/notifications.md): Choose which CloudThinker events reach email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat for your workspace, and who receives them.
- [Workspace Memory](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/memory.md): Browse, correct, and import what CloudThinker remembers about your workspace so agents stop asking for the same context twice
- [Dreaming](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/memory-dreaming.md): Turn on, tune, and run Dreaming, the nightly job that merges duplicates and removes outdated workspace memory and custom skills

## Platform / Admin Settings

- [Admin Settings](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/admin-settings.md): Find every organization setting in one place: members, workspaces, billing, identity, guardrails, audit logs and Workers.
- [Organizations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/organization.md): Set up your CloudThinker organization: rename it, invite teammates, assign roles, and manage seats and member access.
- [Capabilities](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/capabilities.md): Turn Advisor, Blind Spot, and Conversation recaps on or off for one workspace or for your whole organization, and see who can change each setting.
- [Pricing](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/billing/pricing.md): Compare CloudThinker plans, see what each unlocks, and upgrade or start a Team trial from Admin Settings.
- [Manage Your Subscription](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/billing/subscription.md): Change your CloudThinker plan, switch billing interval, add or remove seats, update your card, and download invoices.
- [Usage And Credits](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/billing/usage.md): Read your credit balances, see which runs draw which credits, and track who spends them on the Usage page.
- [Credit Limits](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/billing/credit-limits.md): Set a monthly credit budget per workspace, choose what happens at the limit, and alert the owner before spend runs out.

## Platform / Run anywhere

- [Workers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workers.md): Run a chat or Automation in a folder on your own machine, control what the agent can reach, and keep connection credentials in the cloud.
- [Deployment Options](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/deployment/overview.md): Choose where CloudThinker runs: the hosted cloud, Workers on your own machines, or a private deployment for strict data residency needs.

## Platform / Artifacts and sharing

- [Artifacts](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/artifacts/overview.md): Ask CloudThinker for a report or dashboard from live data, then find, filter, download, and share it from the Artifacts gallery
- [Sharing](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/sharing.md): Publish an artifact as a public link anyone can open without signing in, check what viewers see, and revoke the link at any time

## Enterprise / Security and trust

- [Security and Trust](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/overview.md): Answer a vendor security review: what CloudThinker stores, where agents run, who can act, how writes are approved, and what is logged.
- [Data Protection](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/data-protection.md): Handle a secret caught in chat, read the placeholders agents show in place of secrets, and know what the model sees.
- [Custom Guardrails](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/custom-guardrails.md): Choose which identifiers agents see only as placeholders, lock them for every workspace, and add patterns for your own ID formats.
- [Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/byok.md): Run CloudThinker's AI model calls on your own AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, or FPT Cloud account, set per organization or per workspace.

## Enterprise / Identity and access

- [Set Up Single Sign-On](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/sso.md): Verify your email domain, connect a SAML or OIDC identity provider, choose provisioning, and require SSO for your organization.
- [Set Up SAML SSO](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/sso-saml.md): Connect Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, AWS IAM Identity Center, OneLogin or any SAML 2.0 identity provider.
- [Set Up OIDC SSO](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/sso-oidc.md): Connect Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or any OpenID Connect identity provider to CloudThinker with an issuer URL and client ID.
- [SCIM Provisioning](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/scim.md): Connect your identity provider to CloudThinker with SCIM 2.0 so people are added, suspended, and removed as your directory changes.
- [Roles and Permissions](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/roles.md): Look up what Owner, Admin, Developer, and Viewer can do in your organization and each workspace before you assign a role.

## Enterprise / Governance

- [Audit Logs](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/audit-logs.md): Find out who changed what across your organization, filter events by actor, category, severity and date, and export them as CSV.

## Developers / APIs and integrations

- [Developer Integrations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/api/overview.md): Choose how your systems and tools talk to CloudThinker today: A2A, webhooks, the Claude connector, SCIM and the CLI
- [Claude Connector](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/mcp/overview.md): Connect CloudThinker to Claude to read incidents, costs, code reviews, and security findings, and to start agent runs from a Claude chat
- [Inbound Webhooks](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/webhooks/overview.md): Create a webhook URL that runs an Automation or sends alerts to Resolve, then authenticate, test, and debug it.

## Resources / Learn

- [Introduction: Leadership Edition](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/introduction.md): Get the AgenticOps field guide's argument in ten lines, then pick the chapters that match the decision you need to make.
- [Chapter 1: The Operations Complexity Crisis](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-1-complexity-crisis.md): Understand why modern infrastructure has outgrown human operations teams, and why hiring, scripts and dashboards no longer close the gap.
- [Chapter 2: From Automation to Autonomy](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-2-automation-to-autonomy.md): Trace four generations of operations tooling and learn what an agent platform needs from your stack before it can close the loop.
- [Chapter 3: What Agentic Infrastructure Operations Actually Is](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-3-what-is-aio.md): Define agentic operations, place your team on the L0 to L4 autonomy scale, and test any vendor that claims to sell agents.
- [Chapter 4: Architecture, Multi-Agent Systems for Operations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-4-architecture.md): Learn the multi-agent reference architecture for operations: one orchestrator, scoped specialists, a closed loop, and shared memory.
- [Chapter 5: The Agent Team, Roles and Responsibilities](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-5-agent-team.md): Design an agent team: the core roster, how one incident flows through it, how agents work with humans, and four production case studies.
- [Chapter 6 · Trust, Guardrails, and Governance](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-6-trust-governance.md): Set up the guardrails, data controls, and threat model that let operations agents earn more autonomy without a trust-breaking incident.
- [Chapter 7 · Humans on the Loop: The New Operating Model](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-7-humans-on-the-loop.md): Plan how operations roles change with agents, and raise agent autonomy one proven step at a time without a confidently wrong 3 a.m. action.
- [Chapter 8 · Measuring What Matters](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-8-measuring.md): Measure an agentic operations program with eight KPIs, a three-line business case, per-incident cost tracking, and an agent test harness.
- [Chapter 9 · The Implementation Roadmap](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-9-roadmap.md): Plan agentic operations adoption: check five readiness foundations, run a 90-day pilot with exit criteria, then scale over twelve months.
- [Chapter 10 · The Road Ahead](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-10-road-ahead.md): Plan for five near-term shifts in agentic operations, and choose between hyperscaler-native agents and one platform across every cloud.
- [About CloudThinker](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/about-cloudthinker.md): See how the ideas in this field guide map to CloudThinker features, and start a recommendation-only pilot on your own environment.
- [Introduction · Engineer Edition](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/introduction.md): Get the Engineer Edition's argument on one page, see which chapter answers each adoption blocker, and pick where to start reading.
- [Chapter 1 · The Anatomy of an Operations Agent](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-1-agent-anatomy.md): Break an operations agent into its loop, then judge any platform by its context handling, cost controls, execution rails, and verification.
- [Chapter 2 · Context Engineering: The Real Determinant of Agent Quality](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-2-context-engineering.md): Design the context an operations agent reasons over: five sources, a context budget, memory rules, and discovery that works on day one.
- [Chapter 3 · Tools, Skills, and the Protocol Layer](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-3-tools-skills-protocol.md): Design fewer, intent-shaped tools, encode procedures as skills, and run MCP servers in production without widening your attack surface.
- [Chapter 4 · Orchestration and Two-Engine Economics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-4-orchestration-economics.md): Design agent handoffs, shared incident state, and a two-engine cost model you can measure at your own signal volume.
- [Chapter 5 · The Threat Model: Your Agent Is an Attack Surface](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-5-threat-model.md): Map how prompt injection reaches an operations agent and layer the defenses that keep a hijacked reasoning step contained.
- [Chapter 6 · Policy, Approvals, and Execution Safety as Code](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-6-policy-approvals.md): Classify agent actions by risk, keep the policy as reviewed code, design approvals people read, and record every change so anyone can replay it.
- [Chapter 7 · Evaluating Agents Like Production Systems](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-7-evaluating-agents.md): Read benchmark claims critically, build a test set from your own incidents, score it in layers, and gate every agent change on it.
- [Chapter 8 · Observing the Observer](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-8-observing-the-observer.md): Trace every agent decision, track fleet metrics for quality, latency, cost, drift, and security, and set SLOs that decide autonomy.
- [Chapter 9 · AgentOps: Running the Fleet on Day 2](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-9-agentops-day-2.md): Run an agent fleet after the pilot: versioned releases, model migrations, memory upkeep, blameless agent postmortems, and the weekly role.
- [Chapter 10 · The Vertical Pillars: Complexity, Cost, and Security](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-10-vertical-pillars.md): Tune one agent harness for incidents, cloud cost, and security by adjusting trigger, tempo, context, action risk, and verification cost.
- [Chapter 11 · The Failure Catalog, and Build vs. Buy for Engineers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-11-failure-catalog.md): Spot twelve production failure modes of operations agents by their early signals, apply the fix for each, and decide whether to build or buy.
- [Chapter 12 · Standing Missions: The Autonomous Mission Loop](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-12-autonomous-mission-loop.md): Turn one-off agent chats into narrow standing missions that trigger themselves, verify their own work, and earn autonomy under policy.
- [Appendix A · The POC Test Plan](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-a-poc-test-plan.md): Run a two-to-four-week proof of concept with signed pass/fail gates to test any agentic operations platform against your own incidents.
- [Appendix B · The Agent Platform Engineering Checklist](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-b-engineering-checklist.md): Score a vendor platform or an internal agent build on 38 items across eight surfaces, with the evidence to ask for on each one.
- [Appendix C · Engineer Glossary](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-c-glossary.md): Look up the engineering terms used in this edition, from steps and trajectories to taint tagging and kill switches.
- [Appendix D · Sources and How to Read the Numbers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-d-sources.md): Trace every figure in the Engineer Edition to its primary source, and learn how much weight each kind of number deserves.
- [About CloudThinker · Engineer Edition](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/about-cloudthinker.md): Map each harness layer in the Engineer Edition to the CloudThinker control you can inspect, then run the Appendix A test plan against it.

## Resources / Workshops

- [Prove It Workshop Series](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/workshops/prove-it/overview.md): Plan your Prove It workshop days: the schedule, the rules, what each team hands in, and how to set up CloudThinker before you arrive.
- [Prove It Day 01: Govern](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/workshops/prove-it/day-01-govern.md): Set an agent's boundaries before it works in a cloud account, run a read-only AWS lab on your own account, and write an optimization report you can defend.
- [Prove It Day 02: Investigate](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/workshops/prove-it/day-02-investigate.md): Cut alert noise down to what's worth investigating, test rival hypotheses on a read-only Kubernetes cluster, and write an incident report.
- [Prove It Day 03: Prove It Arena](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/workshops/prove-it/day-03-prove-it-arena.md): Review how the archived Prove It Arena ran: two scored rounds, claim labels, and report skeletons you can reuse.

## Resources / Scenarios

- [Kubernetes Health Monitoring](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/kubernetes-health-monitoring.md): Connect a Kubernetes cluster, check its health in plain language, and investigate a failing pod without running kubectl by hand.
- [Work Across Multiple AWS Accounts](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/multi-aws-accounts.md): Connect several AWS accounts to one workspace, then compare spend and find cost and security issues across them with plain prompts.
- [Investigate a Checkout Incident End to End](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/resolve-checkout-incident.md): Follow one production incident from the first alert to a verified root cause, an approved fix, and a closed incident in Resolve.
- [Catch a Risky Pull Request with Review](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/review-risky-pull-request.md): Watch Review flag a pull request that would break production, question its findings, and land the fix before the change merges.
- [Pentest a Staging App with Cyber](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/cyber-pentest-staging.md): Run a scoped Cyber pentest against a staging app with two test users, read the proof behind each finding, and confirm the fix with a retest.

## Changelog / Changelog

- [Changelog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/changelog.md): Check what changed in each CloudThinker release, newest first, grouped by product with fixes after each release.
